harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s launcher. It now resolves the application directory from its own location, loads the application-owned configuration from any caller working directory, and propagates application exit codes. Existing business output, CentOS 5.11, and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were preserved. The repair survived a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Updated only /srv/legacy2/working-directory-independent-launch/bin/start-report using CentOS 5-compatible POSIX shell syntax.
Verified launches from the application root, /tmp, a directory containing a conflicting config/report.conf, and through PATH.
Induced a controlled application failure and confirmed the launcher returned status 1; restored the configuration and confirmed status 0.
Restarted node1 safely, proved its boot identity changed, and verified the launcher, configuration, output, and platform recovered.

evidence.requirement: Working-directory-independent configuration and preserved business output
evidence.summary: The original output is region=west/report=weekly. After repair, exact output matches from multiple unrelated directories, including one with a conflicting relative configuration.
Pre-change and post-change SHA-1 values for app.py and config/report.conf match; configuration contents and permissions remained intact after reboot.
A controlled application config-read failure produced launcher status 1; after restoration, normal execution produced status 0.

evidence.requirement: Keep installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: CentOS release 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged before and after repair and reboot.

Captured healthy baseline under boot ID d8143a96-f5b8-4e47-8000-000000000000, acknowledged the reboot, proved the new boot ID 2b162e18-6b29-4ad0-8000-000000000000, and verified recovered files and exact application output.
